title: Small-multiples chart of bike-share trips with shared scales
prompt:
Build a small-multiples chart for Spoke & Rail, a city bike-share operator, as one SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 900. The data is trips.csv: monthly trips (in thousands) for six districts from January 2024 to December 2025. An empty cell means the district's stations were closed that month: treat it as no data, never as zero.

Title 'Bike-share trips by district', subtitle 'Monthly trips in thousands, January 2024 to December 2025', footer 'Source: Spoke & Rail trip logs'.

Grid and scales:
- Six equal panels in a 3 by 2 grid, ordered by 2025 total trips from highest (top left) to lowest (bottom right), reading left to right, top row first.
- All panels share one plot-area size and one linear y-scale from 0 to the smallest multiple of 10 that is at least the largest value in the file, with light gridlines every 10. Y tick labels only on the left column; month labels Jan 2024, Jul 2024, Jan 2025, Jul 2025 and Dec 2025 only on the bottom row. The 24 months are evenly spaced, Jan 2024 on the left edge of the plot area and Dec 2025 on the right edge.

Each panel:
- Header: the district name, and under it '2025: <total>k (<change>% vs 2024)' with the 2025 total to one decimal and the signed change to one decimal, for example '2025: 123.4k (+5.6% vs 2024)'. The 2024 total counts reported months only.
- The other five districts as thin light-gray context lines behind, and the panel's own district as a 2.5-unit line in one accent color shared by all panels.
- Missing months break the line (a real gap, no interpolation); a month with no reported neighbour still shows as a dot. Add the note 'Closed Feb–Apr 2024' in the affected panel.
- A dot and label on the district's highest month in the form '12.3k · May 2025' (if the maximum occurs more than once, mark the most recent), and the Dec 2025 value labeled just right of the line's end.
- A dashed horizontal line at the district's 2025 monthly average, labeled like 'avg 12.3'.

Give each panel a group id panel-<district in lowercase with hyphens> (for example panel-old-town) and keep all labels as real text.

rubric.criterion: Panel order is Harbor, Old Town, University (top row, left to right) then Riverside, Airport, Hillcrest (bottom row), in six equal-size panels. (University is listed first in the CSV, so file order is wrong.)

Panel headers show exactly: Harbor '2025: 501.6k (+10.3% vs 2024)', Old Town '2025: 415.7k (+11.1% vs 2024)', University '2025: 408.5k (+4.8% vs 2024)', Riverside '2025: 335.5k (+19.5% vs 2024)', Airport '2025: 291.7k (+69.1% vs 2024)', Hillcrest '2025: 136.3k (-6.9% vs 2024)' (a typographic minus is fine). All six must be right.

Shared scale: every panel's y-axis runs 0 to 60 with gridlines at 0, 10, ..., 60, and line vertices sit at value/60 of the plot height above the baseline within 1% of the plot height. Check at least three vertices in the source, e.g. Harbor Jun 2025 = 56.8, Hillcrest Jan 2025 = 8.1, Airport Dec 2025 = 24.0.

X axis: 24 evenly spaced months with Jan 2024 on the left edge and Dec 2025 on the right edge of every plot area; y tick labels appear only on the left column and the month labels Jan 2024, Jul 2024, Jan 2025, Jul 2025, Dec 2025 only on the bottom row.

Airport's line has a real gap for Feb–Apr 2024 (no zero values, no line bridging the gap), its Jan 2024 value (12.2) is still visible as a dot, the line resumes at May 2024, the same gap appears in the gray Airport context line of the other panels, and the note 'Closed Feb–Apr 2024' is in the Airport panel.

Peak markers are dots with labels on the right months: Harbor '56.8k · Jun 2025', Old Town '46.8k · Jul 2025', University '44.8k · Oct 2025', Riverside '44.7k · Aug 2025', Airport '31.0k · Sep 2025', Hillcrest '15.9k · Jul 2025' (the later of its two 15.9 months, not Aug 2024).
Dec 2025 end labels sit just right of each line end: Harbor 30.6, Old Town 23.0, University 41.6, Riverside 18.9, Airport 24.0, Hillcrest 8.7.

Each panel has a dashed horizontal average line at the correct height, labeled avg 41.8 (Harbor), avg 34.6 (Old Town), avg 34.0 (University), avg 28.0 (Riverside), avg 24.3 (Airport), avg 11.4 (Hillcrest).
Each panel shows the other five districts as thin light-gray context lines behind its highlighted line, and all six highlighted lines use the same accent color and a 2.5-unit stroke.
No collisions: peak labels, end labels, average labels, headers and the closed note do not overlap each other or become unreadable against the lines, and everything fits inside the viewBox.
Title 'Bike-share trips by district', subtitle 'Monthly trips in thousands, January 2024 to December 2025' and footer 'Source: Spoke & Rail trip logs' are present and exact.
File quality: panel groups have the ids panel-harbor, panel-old-town, panel-university, panel-riverside, panel-airport and panel-hillcrest, and all labels are real text elements.

title: Sankey diagram of an energy balance with exact flow widths
prompt:
Draw a Sankey diagram of the Nordvik energy balance as one SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 800, from energy_flows.json (nodes with a column, color and renewable flag, and flows in TWh).

Title 'Nordvik energy balance 2025', subtitle 'From primary source to carrier to end use, TWh'. Under it, one summary line in the form 'Total supply <x> TWh · Renewable share <y>% · Delivered to end uses <z> TWh', computed from the data (renewable share = renewable sources over total supply; delivered = everything except Conversion losses), all to one decimal. Footer 'Source: Nordvik Energy Agency'.

Rules:
- Three columns left to right: sources (column 0), carriers (1), end uses (2). Inside a column keep the node order of the file, top to bottom, with a 20-unit gap between nodes, and center every column vertically on the same horizontal line.
- Scale: exactly 4 units of height per TWh. A node is 24 units wide and as tall as its throughput (the larger of its inflow and outflow).
- Merge flows that repeat the same pair into one ribbon, and leave out flows of zero.
- Each flow is one ribbon whose thickness is 4 units per TWh at both ends, drawn as a smooth band of cubic curves that leaves and enters the nodes horizontally. At every node the ribbons stack flush with no gaps or overlaps, ordered by the position of the node at their other end.
- Ribbons take their source node's color at 35–50% opacity; the Conversion losses node and the ribbons into it are gray with a diagonal hatch pattern.
- Labels: source nodes on their left, like 'Wind 12.5 TWh'; end uses on their right with their share of total supply, like 'Homes 12.3 TWh · 10.1%'; the two carriers labeled so that no ribbon hides them.

Group the file as title, nodes, flows and labels, give each node the id node-<id> and each ribbon the id flow-<from>-<to> (ids from the JSON).

rubric.criterion: Node heights are 4 units per TWh within 1%: Hydro 184, Wind 126, Solar 34, Natural gas 88, Biomass 56, Electricity 412, District heat 76, Homes 158, Industry 138, Services 102, Transport 38, Conversion losses 52. Nodes are 24 wide with 20-unit gaps, and the three columns share one vertical centre (the carrier column starts 30 units lower than the others).

Exactly 15 ribbons connect the right nodes: Hydro, Wind, Solar, Natural gas and Biomass to Electricity; Natural gas and Biomass to District heat; Electricity to Homes, Industry, Services, Transport and Conversion losses; District heat to Homes, Services and Conversion losses. The two gas-to-electricity entries (9.0 and 5.0) form one 14.0 TWh ribbon and there is no Solar to District heat ribbon.

Ribbon thickness is 4 units per TWh at both ends (e.g. Hydro to Electricity 184, Natural gas to Electricity 56, District heat to Services 18) and ribbons stack flush at every node without gaps or overlaps, ordered by their other end (at Electricity's left edge, top to bottom: Hydro, Wind, Solar, Natural gas, Biomass). Verify in the source.
Ribbons are smooth cubic bands that leave and enter nodes horizontally (not straight polygons), filled with the source node's color at partial opacity.

Columns and order follow the file: Hydro, Wind, Solar, Natural gas, Biomass on the left; Electricity above District heat in the middle; Homes, Industry, Services, Transport, Conversion losses on the right.
The summary line reads exactly 'Total supply 122.0 TWh · Renewable share 82.0% · Delivered to end uses 109.0 TWh'.

Source labels on the left read Hydro 46.0 TWh, Wind 31.5 TWh, Solar 8.5 TWh, Natural gas 22.0 TWh and Biomass 14.0 TWh; carrier labels read Electricity 103.0 TWh and District heat 19.0 TWh and are not hidden by ribbons.
End-use labels on the right read Homes 39.5 TWh · 32.4%, Industry 34.5 TWh · 28.3%, Services 25.5 TWh · 20.9%, Transport 9.5 TWh · 7.8% and Conversion losses 13.0 TWh · 10.7%.
The Conversion losses node and its two incoming ribbons are gray with a diagonal hatch pattern; no other ribbon is hatched.

Title 'Nordvik energy balance 2025', subtitle 'From primary source to carrier to end use, TWh' and footer 'Source: Nordvik Energy Agency' are exact; no label overlaps another label or a node, and everything fits inside the viewBox.
File quality: groups title, nodes, flows and labels; node ids like node-hydro and ribbon ids like flow-gas-electricity; text as real text elements.

title: Radial calendar heatmap of 365 days of step counts
prompt:
Make a radial calendar heatmap of one person's daily steps as one SVG with viewBox 0 0 1000 1000, from steps_2025.csv (one row per day of 2025; an empty value means the watch was not worn).

Title 'A year of steps' and subtitle 'Daily step count, 1 January to 31 December 2025' at the top left.

Geometry (exact):
- Centre (500, 520). Month m (1 to 12) owns the 30° sector from (m − 1) × 30° to m × 30°, measured clockwise from 12 o'clock; its day cells span that sector minus 1° of padding on each side.
- Day d of the month is the ring between radius 130 + 8 × (d − 1) and 130 + 8 × d − 1, so day 1 is innermost and day 31 outermost. Draw exactly one cell per real date (no 29 to 31 February and so on).
- Colors by steps: under 4,000 #f1eef6; 4,000–7,999 #bdc9e1; 8,000–11,999 #74a9cf; 12,000–15,999 #2b8cbe; 16,000 and more #045a8d. Days without data: white fill with a thin #9e9e9e outline.
- Every Sunday gets a small dark dot at the centre of its cell.

Labels:
- Outside the outer ring, centred on each sector: the month abbreviation (JAN … DEC) and the month's total in thousands rounded to a whole number, like '123k'.
- In the centre: '2025', then 'Total <n> steps' and 'Daily average <n>' (average over days with data, rounded), with thousands separators.
- Two callouts with leader lines to their cells, which get a thick dark outline: 'Best day: <Ddd DD Mon> · <steps>' and 'Quietest day: <Ddd DD Mon> · <steps>', for example 'Best day: Mon 03 Mar · 12,345'.
- A legend with the five bins, No data and the Sunday dot.

Give each cell the id d-YYYY-MM-DD and keep all text as real text elements.

rubric.criterion: Geometry is exact: 12 sectors of 30° around (500, 520) starting at 12 o'clock and running clockwise, 1° padding at each sector edge, day d spanning radius 130 + 8(d − 1) to 130 + 8d − 1. Spot-check in the source: d-2025-01-01 is the innermost cell just clockwise of 12 o'clock and d-2025-07-19 is ring 19 in the 180°–210° sector (below and left of the centre).
Exactly 365 date cells with ids d-2025-01-01 … d-2025-12-31: February stops at ring 28, April, June, September and November at ring 30, and no cell exists for a non-existent date.
Cells use exactly the five given hex colors with the right bin edges: 3 Mar (7,999) #bdc9e1, 10 May (12,000) #2b8cbe, 12 Oct (16,000) #045a8d, 23 Aug (11,998) #74a9cf, 25 Dec (1,400) #f1eef6.
Exactly the five no-data days (14 and 15 Mar, 2 Aug, 20 and 21 Nov) are white with a thin gray outline.
Exactly 52 Sunday dots, only on Sundays: 5 Jan, 2 Mar, 12 Oct and 28 Dec have one; 4 Jan and 1 Mar (Saturdays) do not.
The centre reads '2025', 'Total 3,395,728 steps' and 'Daily average 9,433'.
Month labels sit outside their own sectors with correct totals: JAN 177k, FEB 215k, MAR 248k, APR 290k, MAY 349k, JUN 362k, JUL 370k, AUG 331k, SEP 317k, OCT 298k, NOV 213k, DEC 225k.
Callouts read 'Best day: Sat 19 Jul · 24,310' and 'Quietest day: Fri 31 Jan · 1,130', each with a leader line ending at its cell, and those two cells have a thick dark outline.

The legend shows the five bins with their ranges and colors, No data and the Sunday dot; the title 'A year of steps' and subtitle 'Daily step count, 1 January to 31 December 2025' are at the top left.
No text overlaps cells, leader lines or other text; month labels, callouts and legend are legible; everything fits inside the viewBox.

title: 24-icon travel set built on a strict construction grid
prompt:
Design Waypoint, a 24-icon set for a travel-planning app, and present it on one specimen sheet: a single SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 960.

Icons, in this order, as a 6 by 4 grid:
Row 1: home, search, map, pin, compass, route
Row 2: plane, train, car, bike, ticket, suitcase
Row 3: sun, cloud, umbrella, snowflake, tent, mountain
Row 4: calendar, clock, bell, bookmark, camera, settings

Construction rules (the source will be checked):
- Define each icon once as a symbol with id icon-<name> and viewBox 0 0 24 24, and place every icon on the sheet with use elements only.
- Keep every point, circle extent and rect edge between 2 and 22 (a 2-unit safe margin; the stroke may overhang by half its width). Put all coordinates on a 0.5 grid. No text and no transforms inside symbols.
- Outline style: fill none, stroke currentColor, stroke width 1.5, round caps and round joins on every icon. The only filled shapes allowed are dots with a radius of 1 or less.
- Every rect uses rx 2 (rx 1 for rects narrower than 6 units).
- Optical size: circular icons fill a 20-unit circle, square ones an 18 by 18 square, wide ones 20 by 16 and tall ones 16 by 20, so all icons look the same size and weight.
- Each icon must be instantly recognisable (for example the bike has two wheels and a frame, the suitcase a handle, the tent a door flap, the settings icon a cog with teeth and a centre hole).

Sheet:
- Header 'Waypoint Icons' with the caption '24 icons · 24 px grid · 1.5 px stroke · round caps'.
- Every icon shown at 72 by 72 (3x), centred in an equal cell, with its name in lowercase underneath.
- Bottom left, a construction panel: the home icon at 192 by 192 over a 24 by 24 grid of unit squares, with the 2-unit margin shaded and the four keylines (circle, square, landscape and portrait rectangles) drawn thinly in red.
- Bottom right, a size ramp: settings at 16, 24, 32 and 48, each labeled with its size.
- Ink #1f2937 on white; grid and keylines in #ef4444 at low opacity.

rubric.criterion: All 24 icons appear in the exact order (home, search, map, pin, compass, route / plane, train, car, bike, ticket, suitcase / sun, cloud, umbrella, snowflake, tent, mountain / calendar, clock, bell, bookmark, camera, settings) in a 6 by 4 grid, each with its lowercase name underneath.

Every icon is instantly recognisable as its name at 72 px (e.g. pin is a teardrop with a hole, route shows a path between two points, bike has two wheels and a frame, snowflake has six-fold symmetry, tent has a door flap, settings is a cog with teeth and a centre hole). Fail if any single icon is ambiguous.

Source structure: 24 symbol elements with ids icon-<name> and viewBox 0 0 24 24, and every placement on the sheet (grid, construction panel, size ramp) is a use element referencing them; no icon geometry is duplicated outside the symbols.
Stroke rules hold in every symbol: fill none, stroke currentColor, stroke-width 1.5, round caps and joins; the only filled shapes are dots with radius 1 or less.

Grid rules hold in every symbol: all points and shape extents between 2 and 22, coordinates on a 0.5 grid, rects with rx 2 (or 1 below 6 units wide), and no text or transform inside symbols. Check at least six symbols.
Optical size is consistent: no icon looks noticeably larger, smaller, heavier or lighter than the others, in line with the circle 20, square 18, landscape 20x16 and portrait 16x20 keylines.
The construction panel shows the home icon at 192 by 192 over a 24 by 24 grid of unit squares, the 2-unit margin shaded, and the four keylines (circle, square, landscape, portrait) thinly in red.
The size ramp shows settings at 16, 24, 32 and 48 units, each labeled with its size, and the stroke scales with the icon (same icon, not redrawn).
The sheet has the header 'Waypoint Icons' and caption '24 icons · 24 px grid · 1.5 px stroke · round caps'; icons are centred in equal cells with even spacing; nothing overlaps or is clipped.

The set looks production-ready: one coherent visual language (same corner treatment, terminal style, detail density and negative space), ink #1f2937 on white, crisp geometry a professional icon designer would ship.

title: Isometric harbor block on an exact tile grid
prompt:
Illustrate Pier 8, a small harbor block, as an isometric SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 900, built on an exact tile grid so every object can be checked.

Grid: an 8 by 8 board of 2:1 isometric tiles. Tile (c, r), with c and r from 0 to 7, is a diamond 96 wide and 48 tall whose top corner is at x = 600 + (c − r) × 48, y = 250 + (c + r) × 24, so the board's corners are (600, 250), (984, 442), (600, 634) and (216, 442). One storey is 32 units straight up. Show every tile outline faintly on the ground and give the board a visible edge thickness.

Ground plan:
- Rows 0 to 2: the Ferry Office on tiles c 0–1, r 0–1 (3 storeys, flat roof with a low parapet, the word FERRY on its left-facing wall); the Warehouse on c 3–5, r 0–2 (2 storeys plus a gable roof whose ridge runs along the c direction and rises one storey above the walls); a clock tower on tile (7, 1) (5 storeys, pyramid cap, a clock face on its left-facing wall).
- Row 3: a plaza with trees on tiles (0, 3), (2, 3), (4, 3) and (6, 3).
- Row 4: a road with a dashed centre line running along the row.
- Row 5: the quay, with street lamps on (1, 5) and (5, 5) and bollards along its front edge.
- Rows 6 and 7: harbor water with a few wave marks and a small boat covering tiles (2, 6) and (3, 6).

Lighting from the upper left: on every box the top face is lightest, the left-facing wall (towards the lower left) mid-tone and the right-facing wall (towards the lower right) darkest, and each object casts a flat shadow on the ground towards the lower right. Draw back to front so nearer objects correctly cover farther ones.

Put the title 'PIER 8' and the line 'Harbor block · isometric study' in the top left. Group each object with an id (ferry-office, warehouse, clock-tower, tree-1 to tree-4, lamp-1, lamp-2, boat) and a data-tile attribute naming its back tile, like data-tile='3,0'. Use a cohesive palette of at most eight hues.

rubric.criterion: The ground grid is exact: 8 by 8 faint tile outlines whose board corners are at (600, 250), (984, 442), (600, 634) and (216, 442) within 3 units (check the source), with a visible board edge thickness below the front edges.

Heights follow 32 units per storey: Ferry Office walls 96 tall with a parapet; Warehouse walls 64 tall with a gable ridge 32 higher running parallel to the c axis (down-right on screen); clock tower 160 tall plus a pyramid cap.

Lighting is consistent on every box, including parapet, roof and small props: top faces lightest, left-facing walls mid-tone, right-facing walls darkest; every object casts a flat ground shadow towards the lower right.

Ground plan matches: four trees on (0, 3), (2, 3), (4, 3), (6, 3); a road along row 4 with a dashed centre line parallel to the c axis; the quay on row 5 with lamps on (1, 5) and (5, 5) and bollards; water on rows 6–7 with wave marks and a boat spanning (2, 6)–(3, 6).
Depth order is correct everywhere: nearer objects cover farther ones and nothing is drawn over something that should hide it; the whole scene fits inside the viewBox.
Details lie in their wall planes: FERRY is sheared onto the Ferry Office's left-facing wall and the clock face is drawn in the plane of the tower's left-facing wall (not a flat front-facing circle).
The title 'PIER 8' and 'Harbor block · isometric study' are in the top left, clear of the artwork.
The illustration is polished: at most eight hues with tints and shades, one consistent line treatment, and detail comparable to professional isometric illustration.
File quality: groups ferry-office, warehouse, clock-tower, tree-1 to tree-4, lamp-1, lamp-2 and boat with correct data-tile values (0,0; 3,0; 7,1; 0,3; 2,3; 4,3; 6,3; 1,5; 5,5; 2,6).

title: Animated four-stroke engine explainer with exact SMIL timing
prompt:
Create an animated explainer of the four-stroke engine cycle for Motorworks Academy as one SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 720 that plays on its own when opened as an image. Use SMIL only (animate, animateTransform, animateMotion, set) with no CSS animation and no script, so the timeline can be scrubbed with setCurrentTime.

Timeline: one master cycle of exactly 8 seconds that repeats forever, split into four 2-second strokes: 1 Intake (0–2 s), 2 Compression (2–4 s), 3 Power (4–6 s), 4 Exhaust (6–8 s). Every animation starts at 0 s and has a duration of 8 s (or 4 s or 2 s) with repeatCount indefinite, so nothing drifts.

Left half, a cross-section of one cylinder:
- The piston is at top dead centre at 0, 4 and 8 s and at bottom dead centre at 2 and 6 s, travelling 120 units with ease-in-out motion (keySplines).
- A crankshaft disc below turns clockwise at constant speed, 720° per cycle, with its crank pin at the top at 0 s; a connecting rod stays attached to both the crank pin and the piston at all times (it may change angle).
- The intake valve (left) opens 14 units during Intake only and the exhaust valve (right) during Exhaust only; both stay closed during Compression and Power.
- The gas above the piston is pale blue during Intake and Compression, bright orange at the start of Power fading to gray by its end, and gray during Exhaust.
- The spark plug flashes (a yellow burst) for 0.3 s starting exactly at 4 s.
- Labels with leader lines: Intake valve, Exhaust valve, Spark plug, Piston, Crankshaft.

Right half:
- Four step cards stacked vertically, each with its number, name and a one-line description; the active stroke's card is highlighted (accent fill and border) exactly during its 2-second window and the others are dimmed.
- A crank-angle readout showing '0–180°', '180–360°', '360–540°' and '540–720°' during strokes 1 to 4.
- A progress bar that fills linearly from empty at 0 s to full at 8 s, with tick marks at each quarter.

Title 'The four-stroke cycle' and subtitle 'One cycle = two crankshaft turns'. Use at most four colors plus neutrals, and give the animated parts the ids piston, crank, rod, intake-valve, exhaust-valve, spark, gas, card-1 to card-4, crank-angle and progress.

rubric.criterion: SMIL only: no script, no CSS @keyframes or animation properties; every animation begins at 0 s with dur 8s (or 4s/2s) and repeatCount indefinite, so all parts stay in sync on an 8-second cycle. To check timing, open the SVG directly in a browser page and scrub it with pauseAnimations() and setCurrentTime(t).

Piston timing: scrubbed frames show the piston at the top at t = 0 and 4 s and at the bottom at t = 2 and 6 s, about 120 units apart, with eased motion (calcMode spline with keySplines, or equivalent values/keyTimes easing).
Cards: at t = 1, 3, 5 and 7 s exactly one card is highlighted, and it is Intake, Compression, Power and Exhaust respectively; the other three are dimmed.
Valves: at t = 1 s the intake valve is open and the exhaust closed; at t = 3 and 5 s both are closed; at t = 7 s the exhaust valve is open and the intake closed.
Spark: the yellow burst is visible at t = 4.1 s and not visible at t = 3.9 s or t = 4.5 s.
Gas color: pale blue at t = 1 and 3 s, bright orange at t = 4.2 s, gray at t = 7 s.
The crank-angle readout shows '0–180°' at t = 1 s, '180–360°' at 3 s, '360–540°' at 5 s and '540–720°' at 7 s.
Progress bar is empty at t = 0, half full at t = 4 s and almost full at t = 7.9 s (linear), with tick marks at each quarter.

Crankshaft: the disc turns clockwise 720° per cycle with the crank pin at the top at t = 0 and at the bottom at t = 2 s, and the connecting rod stays attached to the crank pin and the piston at t = 1 and 3 s.

Title 'The four-stroke cycle', subtitle 'One cycle = two crankshaft turns' and the five part labels with leader lines are present and legible; nothing is clipped or overlapping at any time of the cycle.
Clean technical-illustration style with at most four colors plus neutrals, clear hierarchy and smooth, believable motion.
File quality: the ids piston, crank, rod, intake-valve, exhaust-valve, spark, gas, card-1 to card-4, crank-angle and progress exist on the animated parts.

title: Projected reference map with 20 collision-free place labels
prompt:
Make a reference map of the island nation of Veloria as one SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 860. veloria.geojson holds, in longitude and latitude degrees, the coastline (a MultiPolygon: the main island and an islet), the lake Lago Serpe, the river Fiume Tessa and 20 places with population and a capital flag.

Projection: equirectangular with standard parallel 45°N. A point (lon, lat) maps to x = 40 + (lon − 8) × 180 × cos 45°, y = 120 + (47.5 − lat) × 180. The map frame covers lon 8° to 14° and lat 44° to 47.5° (x 40 to about 803.7, y 120 to 750): clip the map to it and draw a neat line around it.

Content:
- Sea inside the frame; land (both polygons), lake and river drawn from the data with this projection, not redrawn by hand.
- A graticule every whole degree (thin, dashed) with labels outside the frame: 9°E to 13°E along the bottom and 45°N to 47°N along the left.
- Place symbols by class: the capital as a star inside a circle; 250,000 people or more a circle of radius 6; 50,000 to 249,999 radius 4; under 50,000 radius 2.5.
- Labels in sizes by class (capital 17 bold, large 14 semibold, medium 12, small 10.5), each at one of the eight positions around its symbol. No label may overlap another label, a symbol, the river or the frame.
- A scale bar marked 0, 50 and 100 km using 111.2 km per degree of latitude, and a north arrow.
- Right of the frame: the title 'Veloria', the subtitle 'Cities and towns, 2025 census', a legend with the four classes labeled 'Capital', '250,000 and more', '50,000 – 249,999' and 'Under 50,000', the lake and the river, and the note 'Equirectangular projection, standard parallel 45°N'.

Group the file as sea, land, water, graticule, places, labels, scale-bar and legend, and give each place group an id like place-porto-vela.

rubric.criterion: Projection is exact: in the source (after any group transforms) Aurel's symbol centre is at about (444.7, 458.4), Porto Vela at (670.0, 555.6) and Castrano at (173.6, 399.0), each within 2 units.

Geography comes from the data: the main island outline matches the projected coastline, the small islet south-east of the island (centred near (670, 674)) is drawn, Lago Serpe sits north-west of centre, and Fiume Tessa runs from the lake to the southern bay.

All 20 places are labeled with their exact names and no label overlaps another label, a symbol, the river or the frame, including the crowded clusters around Aurel (San Orso, Colvento, Ferrano) and Porto Vela (Brunella, Grazzano).

Symbol classes are right: a star in a circle only for Aurel; radius 6 for Porto Vela, Castrano and Belmira; radius 4 for Valdena, Sorvento, Montecal, Lunara, San Orso and Rivalta; radius 2.5 for the other ten, including Brunella (49,990).
Label sizes follow the classes: Aurel 17 bold, large cities 14 semibold, medium towns 12, small towns 10.5.
Graticule: dashed lines at x ≈ 167.3, 294.6, 421.8, 549.1, 676.4 and y = 210, 390, 570, labeled 9°E to 13°E below the frame and 45°N to 47°N left of it.
The scale bar's 100 km mark is 161.9 units from its 0 mark (within 1%), with 0, 50 and 100 km labels, and a north arrow points up.
Map content is clipped to the frame rectangle from (40, 120) to about (803.7, 750) with a neat line, and the legend and title block sit to the right of the frame without touching it.

Title 'Veloria', subtitle 'Cities and towns, 2025 census', the four legend classes with their exact labels, lake and river entries, and the note 'Equirectangular projection, standard parallel 45°N' are present.
